findings.title: The evaluation does not tell the arms apart: the baseline (v2) already passes the recorded failure on every case
findings.detail: evaluation.json shows baseline and candidate the same on all three cases: missing_placeholders [] and provenance_findings [] for both, pass true for both. Each baseline note.md (v2 prompt, confirmed in the writer transcripts gen-writer-abf27f3b..., gen-writer-a1e7e7ad..., gen-writer-ace5d065...) already cites {{trigger_accession}}, {{cutoff_utc}} and {{price_date}} in Disclosures, and no arm spells dates out in words. The proposal expected the baseline 'to miss at least one of them' on NVDA-0001045810-26-000075-r2, but it did not. 'candidate_fixes_failure_on_all_cases: true' is true only because there is nothing left to fix. There is one sample per arm per case, so the evidence shows no improvement that can be credited to the change.
findings.required_evidence: An evaluation where the parent prompt reproduces the recorded failure on at least the source case, under the same frozen inputs, and the candidate does not

findings.title: The cause of the recorded failure was already removed by a code change, not by a prompt gap
findings.detail: The source-case note (cases/NVDA-0001045810-26-000075-r2/rounds/round-001/generator/note.md, Disclosures) spelled out 'August twenty-sixth, 2026' and left out the accession because its computed/values.json had no trigger_accession, cutoff_utc or price_date keys. Commit 220c535 ('code-supplied disclosure values and frozen evaluation inputs') added those keys in src/aicfinal/values.py lines 37-42. With the keys present, v2 step 5 (policies section 6) is enough, as the baseline runs show. The added prompt text repeats what v2 already gets right.
findings.required_evidence: A case where v2 fails to cite the three keys even though they are present in values.json

findings.title: failure.json uses the cmp-001 ID for a different issue than the one cmp-001 records in the source case
findings.detail: In review-01 and review-02 crit-compliance.json, cmp-001 is the blanket claim 'generated by code from SEC XBRL data', which leaves out the price snapshot (minor, verdict pass). Both critics judged the accession and cutoff omission compliant because publish.py adds them to the published report. The proposal admits this mismatch in 'unresolved'. Adopting a version against a mislabelled failure would make the evolution history misleading, and the real cmp-001 is still unaddressed. Both baseline and candidate notes still use the XBRL-only wording.
findings.required_evidence: A failure record whose ID and description match the critic finding it cites

findings.title: Scope and regression checks pass (recorded so the rejection is not read as a boundary breach)
findings.detail: diff prompts/gen-writer/v2.md vs candidate-change-001.md: the only change is five added lines under Procedure step 5. No acceptance check, gate, threshold, limit, policy or code is changed. Between the prepare commit (582aaa1) and HEAD, only evolution/changes/change-001/* and the candidate prompt changed. The candidate sha256 matches evaluation.json. regressions is [] (held-out AMD case included), and the 53 controller tests pass. Small note: the candidate bans spelling out dates and accessions but not spelled-out rating thresholds ('fifteen percent'). Every arm still writes those in words, which policy and contract allow.

recommendation_note: Reject as unproven, not as harmful. The change is in scope and caused no regression, but the evaluation shows no gain over v2. The disclosure failure it targets went away when code added the disclosure keys (commit 220c535). If the owner wants the wording anyway as a defensive clarification, it carries little risk. A better next change would target the real cmp-001 attribution wording ('SEC XBRL data and the case price snapshot'), with a failure record and evaluation in which the parent actually fails.
